planting.note: Divide and plant in spring or early fall; set crowns with the root-to-foliage junction about 1 inch below soil level.

directions: 'Sebastian on Steroids' produces large, fully double peach-cream blooms with a yellow throat atop tall, well-branched scapes. Flowers are fragrant and the plant reblooms through the season, extending the midsummer show. Grow in full sun for the heaviest bud count and best double form; average, well-drained garden soil is sufficient. This cultivar won the AHS Ida Munson Award for outstanding double-flowered daylilies in 2018.

planting.note: Divide and plant in spring or early fall; set crowns with the root-to-foliage junction about 1 inch below soil level.

directions: 'Sunglasses Needed' bears bright, ruffled lemon-yellow double blooms that nearly glow in midsummer light. The fragrant flowers open in a flat, heavily petaled form and the clump reblooms readily once established. Site in full sun on well-drained soil for the clearest color and tightest ruffling. It received the AHS Ida Munson Award for double-flowered daylilies in 2016.

planting.note: Divide and plant in spring or early fall; set crowns with the root-to-foliage junction about 1 inch below soil level.

directions: 'Sebastian the Crab' opens large apricot-cream double blooms above a green throat, with an unusually high bud count that keeps scapes flowering for weeks. Branching is heavy, so established clumps put on a long midseason display. Plant in full sun with consistent moisture during bud formation for the fullest bloom. This cultivar earned the AHS Ida Munson Award for double-flowered daylilies in 2012.

planting.note: Divide and plant in spring or early fall; set crowns with the root-to-foliage junction about 1 inch below soil level.

directions: 'Back to Black' opens an unusually dark, near-black flower that fades toward chocolate-brown as it ages, often showing a faint cheetah-spotted pattern around a black eye and yellow throat. Blooms are small for the AHS small-flowered class and intensely saturated, making a striking accent among paler daylily companions in the midsummer border. Full sun deepens the dark pigment, while light afternoon shade in hot climates can help prevent sun-bleaching of the petal edges. This cultivar won the AHS Annie T. Giles Award for outstanding small-flowered daylilies in 2025.

common_name: Daylily 'You Are My Sunshine' (Gold with Red Eye)

planting.note: Divide and plant in spring or early fall; set crowns with the root-to-foliage junction about 1 inch below soil level.

directions: 'You Are My Sunshine' bears bright gold-yellow blooms edged and eyed in red above a yellow-green throat, held on well-branched scapes with a high bud count. Flowers stay open longer into the evening than many cultivars, extending the daily display, and the plant reblooms through summer. Grow in full sun on well-drained soil for the cleanest eye-zone contrast. It received the AHS Annie T. Giles Award for small-flowered daylilies in 2018.

common_name: Daylily 'Whistle a Happy Tune' (Cream with Plum Eye)

planting.note: Divide and plant in spring or early fall; set crowns with the root-to-foliage junction about 1 inch below soil level.

directions: 'Whistle a Happy Tune' opens soft cream flowers centered with a plum-purple eye above a green throat, a quietly elegant combination that reads well from a distance. Scapes carry a high bud count across several branches, so established clumps bloom for an extended period and rebloom later in the season. The lightly fragrant flowers open wider and stay open longer than typical daylilies. It earned the AHS Annie T. Giles Award for small-flowered daylilies in 2016.

common_name: Daylily 'Riot on the Kindergarten Bus' (Compact Bright Gold)

planting.note: Divide and plant in spring or early fall; set crowns with the root-to-foliage junction about 1 inch below soil level.

directions: 'Riot on the Kindergarten Bus' is a compact daylily with bright gold self-colored flowers above a green throat, carried on scapes around 20 inches tall that suit border fronts and edging. Semi-evergreen foliage stays low and tidy, and mature clumps rebloom from early into midseason. Its small flower size and modest stature make it a good fit for rock gardens or container plantings in full sun. This cultivar earned the AHS Annie T. Giles Award for small-flowered daylilies in 2013.
